newsitem.title: USA: Hot, dry weather stresses Nebraska dryland corn.
newsitem.headline: Hot, dry weather stresses Nebraska dryland corn.

text.p: The condition of the Nebraska corn crop declined in the week to Sunday as hot, dry weather stressed dryland crops, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Dryland corn was 46 percent good to excellent, down from 66 percent a week earlier. Irrigated corn fell more marginally to 76 percent good to excellent from 80 percent.
"Reports indicated that the irrigated crops looked good, but the condition of dryland acres was beginning to decline due to the dry, hot conditions," the report said.
Grasshopper and corn borer activity was noted.
Seventy percent of the crop had silked, versus 65 percent a year ago and ahead of the 57 percent average pace. Only 27 percent of the crop had silked as of a week ago.
Soybean ratings also declined with 62 percent in the good or excellent category, versus 75 percent a week earlier.

The hot, dry weather provided excellent conditions for the wheat harvest which was 88 percent complete, as of Sunday, up from 79 percent at the same stage last year and a five-year average of 74 percent. Pasture and range conditions were nine percent very poor, 26 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 22 percent good and three percent excellent.
